Quick Vendor Summary

What Is Students First Education Savings Account (ESA)?

Iowa's Students First ESA is open to all Iowa K-12 students regardless of income. Funds equal the state's per-pupil funding amount and are deposited into an Odyssey account. Tuition and fees must be paid first — remaining funds can then go toward tutoring and other qualified expenses.

Important: Iowa ESA requires enrollment in an accredited nonpublic (private) school — homeschool-only families cannot participate directly, and tuition must be paid before other expenses like tutoring. The 2026–27 application window runs April 16 – June 30, 2026.

What Can Iowa ESA Funds Cover?

  • Tutoring and cognitive skills training (after tuition is covered)
  • Tuition and fees at an accredited nonpublic school
  • Textbooks, curriculum, and instructional software
  • Educational therapies for students with disabilities
  • Standardized tests and AP exam fees

How to Apply

Enroll in an accredited private school
This is a separate process from the ESA application itself.
Apply April 16 – June 30
Applications are valid for one school year and must be renewed annually.
Use remaining funds for tutoring
Once tuition is paid through Odyssey, remaining balance can fund tutoring and materials.

Official program source: educate.iowa.gov — ESA Program — always confirm current deadlines and amounts there, since program details can change year to year.

Iowa Students First ESA Tutoring

"The Students First Act, introduced by Governor Reynolds and signed into law on January 24, 2023, makes state funding available to support the success of every K-12 student in Iowa. The bill established a framework and funding for education savings accounts (ESAs), which may be used by eligible families to cover tuition, fees, and other qualified education expenses at accredited nonpublic schools in Iowa. Iowa Administrative Code 281-20 specifies definitions for the program, eligibility requirements for participation, parameters for the application process, and program administration and accountability.
